title: Fine homotopy and tame topology
as_he_states: A homotopy framework should respect algebraic stratifications and tubular-neighborhood behavior.
plausible_today: Choose a definite category of stratified objects and specify the constructibility and equivalence conditions; do not identify every modern stratified theory with this programme.
state_of_art: Cox1978I/II are the cited tubular-neighborhood sources; Esquisse1984§§5–6 supplies the author’s later tame-topology programme, and§7 relates it to Pursuing Stacks.
why_open: The letter explicitly says the Cox papers have not been read; it offers a programme rather than a complete conjecture.
worth: Worth historical comparison once the relevant stratified cotes are available, but too broad for a few-hour theorem task.

title: Weak globular groupoids and the homotopy hypothesis
as_he_states: Weak groupoids, built from freely supplied coherences, should describe homotopy types and be independent of arbitrary coherence choices.
plausible_today: Use a specified Grothendieck coherator convention, intrinsic homotopy-group weak equivalences, and an appropriately truncated or untruncated category of spaces; compare homotopy theories, not just sets of objects.
state_of_art: Ara2013 constructs the fundamental-groupoid comparison on homotopy groups; Henry–Lanari2023 proves the3-dimensional comparison under its precise conventions. OpenAI2026HH claims the all-dimensional Ara–Henry version in Theorem1.1/Corollary5.2; the repository’s Lean scope covers the elementary-expansion part. No independent proof verification or Lean build was performed here.
why_open: The sources identify elementary-expansion stability and the canonical semi-model structure as the difficult step. The manuscript itself highlights coherence choices; no psychological explanation is inferred.
worth: Worth a bounded follow-up only as an exact comparison/audit of conventions and current proof claims, not a fresh attempt to re-solve an unspecified hypothesis.

title: Irredundant coherence operations and rigidity
as_he_states: Are arbitrary coherence stages genuinely new, is the topological realization faithful, and can the primitive part be recovered intrinsically? The automorphism guess is retracted.
plausible_today: Separate three questions: faithful cellular inclusion; faithfulness of a chosen realization; relative automorphism/endomorphism rigidity of a specified free presentation.
state_of_art: Bourke2020 Theorem5.2 proves the first. It does not imply the other two; the source’s invariant notion of operation order and its endomorphism restrictions need an explicit definition before a theorem can be matched.
why_open: The manuscript itself weakens the faithfulness assertion and retracts its automorphism description; later literature cited here treats a distinct formal faithfulness statement.
worth: Worth a short formulation-and-example study because it can prevent false transfers from an established faithfulness theorem.

title: Binary versus arbitrary-arity higher composition
as_he_states: Are binary and n-ary structure descriptions equivalent?
plausible_today: Specify the exact algebraic theory, coherent unit/associativity data, and weak versus strict morphisms before asking for an equivalence.
state_of_art: Mac Lane coherence handles ordinary monoidal categories, and BaezLauda2004 gives a precise weak/coherent2-group comparison; neither alone resolves all higher conventions in the aside.
why_open: The source does not fix the morphism category, so an exact theorem is not recoverable from the question as written.
worth: Low priority unless another source supplies the missing conventions.

title: Which model-category hypotheses make the globular construction work?
as_he_states: Replace topological disks by model-category resolutions; the fibrancy of pushouts is questioned.
plausible_today: Assume the ambient model category has all objects fibrant, or make fibrant replacements and coherence choices explicit; do not infer fibrancy merely from cofibrations between contractible Kan objects.
state_of_art: Ara2013Homotopy Theorem8.7 gives the precise homotopy-group comparison. CL-SA24-015 supplies a complete Kan counterexample to the unqualified pushout claim.
why_open: The manuscript footnote already identifies the fibrancy issue; no further historical reason is asserted.
worth: Useful as a short explanatory correction and test case, with little remaining novelty in the basic counterexample.

title: Unfinished converse Hom formula and slice sketches
as_he_states: The reverse Hom_D(M,L) and several slice/comma comparison expressions are unfinished.
plausible_today: The degree-zero-to-complex direction requires the actual derived Hom/Ext data; the slice comparison needs its coefficient and variance conventions fixed.
state_of_art: Standard derived adjunction and category-of-elements homology give possible frameworks, but no unique missing formula can be recovered from these pages.
why_open: The relevant right-hand sides are simply absent.
worth: Moderate interpretive value: recover notation from adjoining manuscript pages before assigning a new research conjecture.

title: Abstract linearization from a tensor contractor
as_he_states: Do hypothesesa–d force M[W⁻¹]≃D_{≥0}(Mod_k)? The theorem is marked(?) and the contractible-projective counit case is left A prouver.
plausible_today: Retain every categorical, exactness and universal tensor hypothesis; distinguish the original a–d version from the strengthened resolving-functor/flat-unit version on scan55. A plausible precise target is the all-complex counit criterion under additional homotopy compatibility of the resolving adjunction.
state_of_art: CL-SA24-030 states the exact verified later scope. General arbitrary-k monoidal sufficiency is not certified by the sources located.
why_open: PS§135 says the author was unsure whether he would answer the questions; no source explains the history of this specific undated draft. The missing contraction-compatibility step is visible, not a psychological explanation.
worth: High interest: isolate whether the displayed hypotheses entail the missing counit test before attempting a broader new theorem.

title: Projectivity after tensoring a resolution
as_he_states: Are J⊗L_i projective?
plausible_today: It is enough that J⊗− be exact and carry projectives to φ-acyclic objects. Flatness alone is not the needed projectivity claim.
state_of_art: Classical derived-composite and acyclic-resolution theorem, dual of Tohoku§2.4 Theorem2.4.1/Remark3, gives the exact replacement.
why_open: The page itself asks the question; no historical source for abandonment was found.
worth: A short audit can settle the intended presheaf examples and identify precisely where projectivity can be weakened.

title: Universal tensor preservation of abelian weak equivalences
as_he_states: After identifying φ(ξ)≃φ(η) with a derived equivalence, the page proposes F⊗ξ→F⊗η as an abelian weak equivalence.
plausible_today: Retain φ-acyclic/projective restrictions on ξ,η and require an actual tensor-homotopy or derived-flatness argument for arbitrary F.
state_of_art: K-flatness gives the classical chain-level result; the modern homological presheaf model structures do not by themselves settle every displayed abstract tensor comparison.
why_open: The label qu.is is crossed out and replaced by abelian weak equivalence; the full argument is not written.
worth: Moderate interest: test the exact quantifiers against the chosen resolving functor before asking for a general monoidal localization.

title: Descent of the adjunction through localization
as_he_states: If the localized right functor exists, do the two localized functors remain adjoint?
plausible_today: Yes when it is the functor induced by G preserving the chosen weak class, with F likewise compatible; the original unit/counit then localize.
state_of_art: Maltsiniotis2020 Lemma2.1.6 is an exact affirmative result for this typed question.
why_open: The source question is formal, with an inconsistent star/subscript notation. No deeper unresolved obstruction is asserted.
worth: Low research interest: resolve the notation and cite the established localization lemma.

title: All-complex counit and reduced test objects
as_he_states: The page lists equivalence, all counits quasi-isomorphisms, projective counits, and degree-zero/acyclic projective tests as equivalent.
plausible_today: The formal reductions hold under exactness and enough projectives; the remaining task is to prove the acyclic test from the contractor assumptions.
state_of_art: CL-SA24-040 gives the exact formal result; CL-SA24-041 gives the standard double-resolution reduction. Hubert2025 Remark4.2.7 concerns a related weaker test and does not erase this remaining implication.
why_open: The degree-zero step is followed by OK, then the acyclic case by A prouver. This precise gap, rather than the whole formal criterion, is documented.
worth: High interest: a complete map of the unit/counit and homotopy operations would make the draft’s genuinely missing step explicit.

title: Global versus universal asphericity of the interval
as_he_states: An aspherical I is said to have a tensor-acyclic augmentation kernel; J is later called totally aspherical after an all-coefficient test.
plausible_today: Use a universal/local asphericity premise, or directly demand Lφ(J⊗x)=0 for allx. Global object asphericity is insufficient, even with separated multiplicative endpoints.
state_of_art: The finite counterexample in outputs/core_computations.json checks the weaker interpretation; Maltsiniotis’s local/global definitions explain the distinction.
why_open: The word sur is deleted on the lemma line, and the stronger phrase occurs just above it. The reason for this change is not supplied.
worth: High interpretive value: a scan check of the exact relative adjective could change which mathematical assertion the leaf makes.

title: Perfect pairing for opposite augmentation units
as_he_states: Does j′!x=Hom_M(x,1_M) agree with Hom_(M^op)(x^op,1_(M^op))∨, through the displayed pairing?
plausible_today: Specify both representing units and a natural perfect pairing of their Hom functors; then finite-projective biduality yields the desired comparison. Without those data there is no universal theorem to assert.
state_of_art: SGA6 I7.2–7.3 and Stacks07VI prove biduality for perfect complexes. PS §139 discusses the related homology/cohomology program but does not identify the units of this leaf. Searches did not locate an exact general answer with its unspecified notation.
why_open: The source leaves a question mark and does not fix the two objects; no external source found documents a later abandonment.
worth: Worth a focused reconstruction only after the small category and its two unit objects are fixed, because a perfect-pairing criterion is then testable.

title: Transfer of universal interval acyclicity
as_he_states: A compatible map J′→J of augmented bicoaugmented objects should transfer the universal tensor-weak augmentation from the multiplicative interval J to J′.
plausible_today: The literal assertion is false. A sufficient repair is that the comparison itself be universally tensor-weak (REF-LATE-1), or that J′ carry a suitable compatible contraction. Neither extra hypothesis is asserted to be in the ink.
state_of_art: Explicit DGA counterexample and all category/endpoint/tensor hypotheses are in late_proof_checks.md with saved computations. Hubert2026 proves a different statement for strong Whitehead test categories; PS §134 poses the larger interval/homotopy program. No primary source for the literal transfer was located.
why_open: The transcribed prose and diagram reverse the comparison arrow, and the written assumptions admit extra homology summands. There is no located historical explanation of how the author intended to repair this.
worth: High value for one reconstruction run: check the original ink for a missing weak-equivalence or contraction condition before developing a new theorem.

title: A small chain diagonal left adjoint to totalization
as_he_states: The small chain category is to map into a double chain category; the proposed Hom adjunction and the target membership of δ(L) carry question marks.
plausible_today: For nonnegative homological k-complexes and first-quadrant commuting bicomplexes, the signed finite-diagonal functor on the small diagram categories gives Tot as restriction and its left Kan extension as left adjoint. Preservation of the manuscript’s particular small subcategory/completion is an additional question.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: CL-SA24-056, CL-SA24-057, CL-SA24-063 give an explicit verification. Tohoku §1.7(e) is the diagram-category antecedent. Riehl Cor6.2.9 supplies Kan adjoints. The opened2026 inflation paper, Theorem3.5/Remark3.7, treats a characteristic-zero cochain/Bigolin framework and is a related special comparison, not a theorem about every completion.
why_open: The page itself leaves the small-category target and completion undecided. No source found states a historical reason that he dropped it.
worth: Worth a short precise reconstruction of the small subcategory once the completion glyphs are checked; existence on full first-quadrant module categories is already resolved.

title: Recover ordinary categories from exponential additive objects
as_he_states: Objects satisfying δ(a)≃a⊗a and κ(a)≃k are to play a special role; the candidate N and internal-Hom comparison remain fragmentary.
plausible_today: Fix an augmented coherent comultiplicative additive envelope, define exponential objects including their coherence data, and specify a comparison with the original category. Arbitrary isomorphisms of the displayed shapes are not enough.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: PS VII§139 originalpp590–591 gives the exact typed reconstruction hope. CL-SA24-079 records targeted searches and separates the specific S¹/Tannakian comparison in Toën2020 Cor3.5 from this unformulated general theorem.
why_open: The typed source explicitly says the relevant operations have not been worked out; the handwritten fragment also omits necessary definitions. No stronger explanation is documented.
worth: Worth a separate definitional task after checking the envelope notation; a broad reconstruction theorem is not presently a well-defined claim here.

title: Binomial models for integral Eilenberg–MacLane cochains
as_he_states: The handwritten fragment places K(Z,n), Symbin and a derived marker beside binomial polynomials; the exact typed question is in PS VI§119 originalpp503–504.
plausible_today: For n≥1 use the canonical map Symbin(Z[−n])→Z^{K(Z,n)} or its derived-binomial version. Broader space reconstruction needs the stated connected nilpotent finite-type hypotheses, with a different completion/localization statement outside them.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Horel2024 Prop4.2 proves the exact cosimplicial comparison. KSZ2026 Prop3.6/Example3.7 gives LBin(Z[−n])≃C*(K(Z,n),Z). Ekedahl2002 Thm2.9 gives numerical models under finite-type nilpotence; Toën2020 Cor3.4 gives the K(Z,n) affinization. These are matched statements, not an “all spaces” theorem.
why_open: The handwritten page provides no historical explanation. PS§119 identifies the integral obstruction to naive polynomial models and proposes numerical/binomial replacements; that mathematical motivation is documented.
worth: Worth a comparison commentary connecting the exact source map to the established constructions; do not present the K(Z,n) case as an unsolved conjecture.

title: The augmented additive Theorem A implication graph
as_he_states: Representable tests, all coefficients, ordinary-looking counits, W-preservation/reflection, aspherical objects and localized equivalence are compared; reverse arrows carry extra asphericity and epimorphism hypotheses.
plausible_today: Use derived counits and derived unit asphericity, a precise additive module completion and projective-augmentation assumptions. Prove each reverse implication separately. Localized equivalence requires additional full-faithfulness and essential-surjectivity input.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: CL-SA24-082, CL-SA24-083, CL-SA24-084, CL-SA24-085, CL-SA24-086 give the verified representable-resolution implication, the formal W consequence, and a BZ→e counterexample to the ordinary counit and ordinary-unit-asphericity readings. Hubert2026 Prop4.6 is exact for ordinary category presheaves; its model/localization results have additional test/strong-Whitehead assumptions.
why_open: The unfinished proof, deleted isomorphism sign and separately written hypotheses are visible. No source says precisely why the complete graph was not carried through.
worth: Worth a single theorem audit with a corrected typed graph and countermodels for each omitted hypothesis; this is the most efficient substantive next task.

title: Monoidal Eilenberg–Zilber compatibility of the comparison
as_he_states: Whether the λ! tensor comparison is a quasi-isomorphism and λ*(L⊗M)↔λ*L⊗λ*M lies in W_M; the triangle is labelled EZ and its top arrow remains questioned.
plausible_today: Specify a coherent diagonal on M, homotopical tensor products, and an adjunction whose counit and comparison maps satisfy the stated triangle. In the classical simplicial-chain case the Alexander–Whitney/shuffle comparison is a chain homotopy equivalence.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Eilenberg–Zilber1953, printedp201, proves the classical product-chain equivalence. CL-SA24-062, CL-SA24-063, CL-SA24-064 separate that case from arbitrary M. Hubert2026’s strong-Whitehead comparison does not by itself supply the whole monoidal structure.
why_open: Missing comparison data are visible in the diagrams. No opened source establishes why this particular development was not completed.
worth: Worth a focused run on the exact minimal diagonal and acyclicity hypotheses, since the general monoidal assertion is stronger than the available additive comparison.

title: The Φ interval, exterior powers and K-grid construction
as_he_states: The page sketches Φ/k, an apparent short sequence ending in K[1,Z], its exterior/tensor powers, and K_{p,q} on p+q=n+1; it supplies no full definitions.
plausible_today: First identify Φ, all maps and the intended complex convention from the scans or related leaves. Only then ask for exactness, acyclicity or comparison with normalized chains.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Dold1958 Theorem1.9 identifies the normalization arrow; CL-SA24-058, CL-SA24-060 show that this does not identify the extra Φ and K data. Searches of Dold–Kan, totalization and EZ sources found no exact formulation of these fragments.
why_open: The source is fragmentary, rather than a well-formed modern open problem. No historical account of abandonment was found.
worth: Worth a transcription/context reconstruction before a research task is cut; the present text does not support a new conjecture.

title: Exact coefficient functors and derived sections
as_he_states: The page asks whether exact u commutes with RΓ and whether u(C) is acyclic or injective; the Hom(a,−) test and flat/coflat conditions are developed.
plausible_today: Require uΓ≅Γ′u and preservation of Γ′-acyclic resolutions. For u=Hom(P,−), projectivity, k-flatness, tensors/cotensors and enough injectives give a bounded-below theorem. Arbitrary exact u does not suffice.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: The acyclic-composition criterion is Tohoku §2.4 Thm2.4.1, with modern Stacks13.22.1. CL-SA24-065, CL-SA24-066, CL-SA24-068, CL-SA24-072 recheck the precise sufficient conditions and give an exact rationalization/product counterexample.
why_open: The author explicitly asks about acyclicity and injectivity. A historical reason for leaving the step unresolved is not documented by the opened sources.
worth: Worth a short clean statement with all coefficient hypotheses; the broad exactness-only form is already excluded.

title: Can injective dualization produce projectives?
as_he_states: The desired dual coefficient functor Hom(−,ξ) should send injectives to injectives of the opposite category, hence projectives in the original one.
plausible_today: Restrict to a coefficient category with an actual projective-injective duality, or classify rings and designated dualizing objects satisfying this property. It is false for arbitrary injective ξ over Z.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: CL-SA24-067 independently refutes the universal version using I=ξ=Q. Stacks15.55.1 verifies the injectivity premise. Semisimple coefficient categories give easy positive cases; no full classification is claimed.
why_open: The needed injective-to-projective property is visibly questioned. No source found attributes an historical abandonment to this counterexample.
worth: Worth considering only after a concrete restricted coefficient category is specified; the universal proposal is false.

title: Asphericity with general abelian coefficients
as_he_states: Comma-category homological asphericity should imply comparison for all coefficients in a k-additive category with enough projectives; a coaspherical/injective version is then pursued under stronger assumptions.
plausible_today: For module presheaves use k-acyclic A/b for homology, or b/A for cohomology. For general coefficients explicitly supply completeness/cocompleteness, tensors/cotensors, enough suitable projectives/injectives, and the acyclicity needed by the comparison.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Hubert2026 Prop4.6 gives the exact integral representable/all-presheaf theorem and W-reflection consequence. CL-SA24-071 proves the stronger cohomological coefficient reduction through Hom(P,−). The bare scan68 hypothesis list is not enough to invoke that proof without additions.
why_open: The source itself experiments with the missing coefficient hypotheses. No independent historical account of why it stayed open was located.
worth: Worth a precise coefficient-general theorem and a list of failures when one hypothesis is removed; the ordinary module case is established.

title: When is the augmentation unit a weak equivalence?
as_he_states: The unit y→κ*κ!y is marked W_M?; applying κ! gives an arrow marked iso? in the triangle.
plausible_today: For an adjunction L⊣R with invertible counit and W detected by L, every unit is in W. The homological use must be formulated for derived adjoints and a derived counit.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: CL-SA24-075, CL-SA24-076 prove the formal triangle argument. CL-SA24-083 excludes replacing the derived counit by its ordinary counterpart. Hubert2025/2026 gives exact comparison equivalences with additional hypotheses.
why_open: The manuscript puts the invertibility and weak-equivalence questions on the arrows. The sources do not provide a historical explanation of the unfinished formulation.
worth: Worth a concise reconstruction coordinated with the general comparison theorem; the abstract implication is already formal.

preserved_discrepancies: Retain scan73 as the questioned occurrence and scan77 as the subsequent rank calculation.
The finite-projective local-rank≤1 classification applies to the module example, not every adjoint triple.
Keep the further-adjoint existence question as a distinct subquestion.
merge_notes.integration: Consolidate as one problem with distinct source-specific subquestions, occurrences, conditional results, and unresolved maps. This is not a claim that all variants are equivalent.

title: Represent F by an exact slice with projective unit
as_he_states: Seek f:N→M with f! exact, 1_N projective and f!1_N=F; then narrow to 1_N∈N and target a∈M.
plausible_today: The ordinary presheaf interpretation forces F projective because restriction is exact. Representables are realized by the ordinary slice A/a→A. A further projective/retract generalization needs the relevant additive/idempotent completion and unit structure stated.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: CL-SA24-074, CL-SA24-078 prove the representable construction and the general projectivity obstruction. PS VII§135 originalp564 formula(11) supplies the exact typed slice case. An arbitrary flat F is still insufficient, as Q over Z shows.
why_open: The page itself narrows the target after the initial requirements. The source does not say that the projectivity obstruction motivated that change; that would be an inference.
worth: Worth a bounded classification of realizable small/projective targets; an arbitrary-object construction of the stated kind is impossible.

title: Geometric nonabelian extension obstructions
as_he_states: Relate Gr-category splitting geometrically to Mac Lane kernels and group extensions; ask whether everyH³ class occurs.
plausible_today: Use pinned group-module data and distinguish an ordinary monoidal2-group, a relative2-gerbe overBG, and its higher morphisms.
state_of_art: The realization question is classically positive (MacLaneHomology IV§9, with the all-group reference to Eilenberg–MacLane1947). Breen1994§§6–7 develops the2-gerbe/Gr-stack geometry; BaezLauda2004 Theorem43 gives explicit cocycle equations.
why_open: The leaf seeks a direct geometric explanation of an invariant it already calls classical; no claim of modern openness is retained.
worth: Worth a short translation companion, not a new existence theorem.

title: Picard functors with fixed homotopy-group maps
as_he_states: When do identical maps onπ0,π1 imply isomorphic functors, and when do prescribed maps lift?
plausible_today: For fixed compatible invariant maps, retain theExt² obstruction and, when it vanishes, theExt¹ torsor andHom automorphisms; distinguish global and internal Ext on a topos.
state_of_art: SGA4XVIII1.4.15–1.4.18 gives the derived description. The finiteC2 example in CL-SA24-110 refutes the first unqualified sentence, which the source itself immediately qualifies.
why_open: This is a correction already visible within the manuscript, not an unresolved research gap.
worth: High value for the folder commentary because a one-line oversimplification otherwise destroys the functor classification.

title: Realizing sheaf Picard invariants and the universal Ext³ claim
as_he_states: Does every triple(M,N,σ:M→N[2]) on a topos come from a Picard stack? The notes first constructob(σ), then assert its universal vanishing.
plausible_today: Identifyob(σ) with the connecting morphism in Breen’s low-degree sequence; test the claimed universal classifying-topos Ext-vanishing under exactly the author’s category and pinning conventions.
state_of_art: Breen1994§7.9(7.9.2) recordsExt²→H⁵(K(M,3),N)→Hom(M/2M,N)→Ext³. Ordinary groups realize everyσ by CL-SA24-102, but that basis argument is not a global sheaf argument. No nonzero boundary is inferred just from a nonzeroExt³ group.
why_open: The source leaves the universal Ext calculation unexpanded. The consulted later source retains the boundary; this alone does not prove that the boundary is ever nonzero. The remaining uncertainty is the outcome of this dossier’s recorded searches, not a claim of a presently open problem.
worth: High priority for a sharply bounded source-and-obstruction check because it determines whether the displayed short exact sequence is justified.

title: Automorphisms of the split Gr-category
as_he_states: What are the invariants of its Gr-category of self-equivalences?
plausible_today: For ordinary monoidal functors and monoidal natural transformations, useH² for equivalence classes andZ¹ for automorphisms; introduce0-cochain modifications only if a3-categorical mapping object is intended.
state_of_art: BaezLauda2004 Theorem43 yields the cochain model; CL-SA24-113 gives the explicit calculation and identifies the missing action in the split tensor formula.
why_open: The handwritten question does not distinguish the ordinary mapping groupoid from its higher modification enhancement.
worth: Worth a small dictionary with an explicit nontrivial-action example, with the main classification already known.

title: Strictification and enriched composition
as_he_states: Can weak higher categories be replaced by strict ones, and do the kernel-composition and Hom-wise equivalence tests capture the intended higher structure?
plausible_today: Separate fully strict globular models from semistrict models; state representability assumptions for strong kernel composition; add essential surjectivity to the Hom-wise equivalence criterion.
state_of_art: Ara2013Strict gives the strict-model obstruction. Kelly1982 gives density/coends and enriched equivalence criteria. The two-object discrete target is a complete counterexample to Hom-wise equivalence alone.
why_open: Several distinct notions of strictness and equivalence appear in the sketch without final definitions; the modern answers depend on those choices.
worth: Moderate priority as a formulation audit, with a few-hour run able to produce exact corrected statements.

title: Stackification, inverse images and site invariance
as_he_states: Build enveloping n-stacks, compare a site with its topos, and obtain inverse images by adjunction.
plausible_today: For groupoidal n-stacks use truncated sheaves of spaces and geometric morphisms; for category-valued higher stacks specify a presentable higher category of coefficients and descent convention.
state_of_art: LurieHTT6.2.2.7 and6.5.2.14 give the precise sheafification/local-model comparison. Finite truncation avoids confusing ordinary descent with unbounded hyperdescent.
why_open: The pages are an agenda rather than an axiomatically fixed theory; the modern sources make choices that must be recorded.
worth: Useful for a source companion, but a broad reconstruction would exceed one research run.

title: Base change, depth and Lefschetz for higher stacks
as_he_states: Seek constructible higher-stack analogues of base-change and Lefschetz theorems, with a notion of depth along a closed subset.
plausible_today: First fix topology, morphism class, constructibility, truncation degree and a precise connectivity conclusion.
state_of_art: SGA4 supplies the classical background and LurieHTT supplies a higher-topos language; no exact theorem can be matched to the unquantified headings alone.
why_open: No reason for abandonment is stated; the absence of definitions on these leaves is not evidence that the whole programme was abandoned.
worth: Low priority until a more explicit occurrence is found in another supplied or later source.

title: Locally constant higher stacks and the shape of a topos
as_he_states: Recover a completed homotopy type from all locally constant n-stacks and their truncation maps.
plausible_today: Specify whether the target is shape, protruncated shape or a completion at finite/group-theoretic coefficients; retain the sections functor and compatibility data.
state_of_art: LurieHTT7.1.6.3 and7.1.6.9 give a precise shape construction and explain the Artin–Mazur/truncation distinction.
why_open: The author explicitly asks for suitable constructibility restrictions; the source does not choose them.
worth: Moderate priority: a short run can state an exact comparison theorem under fixed local-connectedness and finiteness assumptions.

title: Higher Picard stacks, coefficients and derived operations
as_he_states: Classify strict and non-strict Picard n-stacks, extend to ring coefficients, and interpret derived Hom/tensor geometrically.
plausible_today: Use enhanced truncated complexes for the strictly commutative linear theory and connective truncated spectra for the general symmetric theory; define strictness explicitly.
state_of_art: SGA4XVIII1.4 gives the1-stack operations; Tatar2011 Theorem6.4 gives strict Picard2-stacks; GJO2019 gives stable2-types, while GJOS2017 computes only part of the Postnikov data and proves a strict-skeletal obstruction.
why_open: The source says n≥2 is unknown to the author. Later papers explain that higher Postnikov interactions prevent naïve skeletal strictification.
worth: High conceptual value, but a few-hour task should only build the precise n=2 comparison dictionary.

title: Higher Picard envelopes and algebraic K-theory
as_he_states: Extend the Picard-envelope interpretation ofK0,K1 to higherK-groups and understand the obstruction to a canonical linear complex.
plausible_today: Distinguish object inversion from groupoidification, split from exact K-theory, and a spectrum/Picard model from a mere complex with the same homology.
state_of_art: Segal1974 supplies spectra from categorical addition; MuroTonks2007 gives the1-type andη formula; MuroTonksWitte2015 supplies universal determinant targets.
why_open: The notes themselves point to the nontrivial commutativity invariant. Modern theory identifies it with stableη rather than an unexplained failure of linear algebra.
worth: High expository value: a short run can make the low-degree comparison fully explicit and prevent overgeneralization to arbitrary exact K-theory.

title: Recovering the isolated homotopy-fiber diagrams
as_he_states: Complete the Γ_f comparison diagrams and their weak universal properties.
plausible_today: Recover the source’s category and notation first, then formulate the corresponding homotopy-pullback statements with choices and connectivity assumptions.
state_of_art: Quillen1967 gives a standard pointed homotopy framework, but the supplied diagram fragments do not identify every intended arrow.
why_open: The needed definitions are not on these isolated leaves; no historical conclusion follows from that packet boundary.
worth: Low priority before a scan/context pass, since inventing the missing notation would defeat the purpose.

title: Two-operation categorical rings and their invariants
as_he_states: Which invariants besidesπ0 as a ring andπ1 as a module classify the two-operation Picard structure?
plausible_today: Use a degree-three distributivity/associativity class together with multiplicative symmetry data and impose the symmetry equation on its braiding cocycle.
state_of_art: JibladzePirashvili2007 gives MacLaneH³ for categorical rings; QuangHanh2015 Theorems6.1–6.2 and§3 give the braided classification and the symmetric restrictionβ(x,y)+β(y,x)=0.
why_open: The manuscript leaves the coherence axioms open; later definitions make those axioms explicit. No claim about why the author stopped is inferred.
worth: Moderate priority for an exact axioms-to-cocycle translation; the broad classification direction is already developed.

title: Simplifying Sính’s Picard complex and fraction presentation
as_he_states: Identify simpler invariants forH²(Hom(L′(M),N)) and check the quotient/fraction composition and universal property.
plausible_today: For ordinary groups, identify the diagonal invariantσ:M→N[2]; for sheaves retain theExt²/Ext³ terms. State quotient congruence closure and a2-universal equivalence of functor categories.
state_of_art: The French summaryscan43 states the ordinary invariant answer. Sính1975 is the exact construction source; Breen1994§7.9 explains the sheaf distinction, and modern determinant constructions give a comparison target.
why_open: The English margin asks for a simplification already described in the French summary; their order does not establish chronology.
worth: Worth a small explicit comparison of the complexes and the two summaries, without claiming a new classification.

title: Stabilization and symmetric monoidal compatibility
as_he_states: Does the canonical comparison fail to be faithful for S¹, preventing a compatible ACU structure?
plausible_today: The conditional universal-property implication is valid, but the asserted S¹ example is false: its cyclic3-permutation is trivial in the homotopy category, so ordinary symmetric monoidal stabilization exists.
state_of_art: Robalo2015 Theorem2.14 gives the exact ordinary symmetric monoidal stabilization theorem, with no finite-CW premise; S¹ satisfies its cyclic3-permutation condition. FreydStable1966 is the cited historical suspension comparison. The conditional obstruction is independently re-proved; the asserted example is refuted.
why_open: The source does not verify its asserted nonfaithfulness example. The universal-property conditional itself is sound; no explanation of the mistaken example is inferred.
worth: Worth a focused correction because the claimed obstruction is conceptually misleading.
